history.p: In 1856 Gade started composing a violin concerto in A Minor; however, only the solo part of the first movement has survived (DK-Kk C II, 27). In 1871 he donated the manuscript to the physician Heinrich Lehmann with the remark: "Ja videre kom jeg ikke paa Grund af knap Tid - en anden Gang mere!" (Well, I didn't get any further due to lack of time - another time some more), but it was not until the summer of 1880 that he composed an entirely new violin concerto. On 23 December he sent the score and solo part to Joseph Joachim, whom he knew from his time in Leipzig, in order to hear his opinion. The latter was so delighted that he asked for Gade's permission to try it out with his orchestra at Hochschule für Musik in Berlin, where he was teaching. The first performance on 15 February 1881 was a success, but Joachim never played it again. Gade also send a copy to the famous Czech violinist Wilma Neruda, whose brother Franz Neruda lived and worked in Copenhagen, but although she praised the concerto in a letter to Gade, she apparently never played it in public either. Nevertheless it was performed a number of times, mainly in Germany, during the last decade of Gade's life.
